questions.q: What does turning on Debug mode actually spin up?
options: A live Spark cluster you can interactively test transformations against
A new Azure SQL Database instance
A self-hosted integration runtime
Nothing — Debug mode is purely a static preview with no compute
questions.explain: Debug mode starts a real Spark cluster (AutoResolveIntegrationRuntime by default) so you can interactively preview transformations as you build.

questions.q: What does the time to live (TTL) setting control?
options: How long the debug cluster stays warm after activity stops before shutting down
How many rows Data Preview shows
How long a pipeline trigger stays active
The maximum number of transformations in a data flow
questions.explain: TTL defaults to 60 minutes — raising it gives more idle time before the session times out, useful during a long design session.

questions.q: Does a debug session write data to the data flow's sink?
options: No — debug mode never writes to a sink; it's a test harness for transformation logic only
Yes, every debug run fully writes to every configured sink
Only if the sink is Azure Blob Storage
Only if Allow schema drift is enabled
questions.explain: Sinks are ignored during debug. To confirm a sink actually works, you run the data flow from a pipeline instead — the pipeline's own Debug button or a real trigger.

questions.q: What does the row limit in Data Preview come from?
options: Debug Settings, which overrides any sampling configured in the source transformation while debug is on
The dataset's own schema definition
The pipeline's timeout setting
It always shows every row in the source, with no limit
questions.explain: Debug Settings sets a row limit per source, and it takes precedence over the source transformation's own sampling setting during a debug session.

questions.q: How is a debug session billed?
options: Hourly, for the entire time it runs, including TTL idle time — turn it off when you're done
It's completely free, with no billing at all
Only billed if a sink is actually written to
Billed per row previewed, not per hour
questions.explain: Every debug session spins up its own Spark cluster and is billed hourly for the whole time it's running, including idle TTL time — a real reason to turn it off when finished.
